observation_summary: The compiler fails to identify void functions, defaulting to '?' instead of 'undefined'. The fix involves adding a new capability to infer return statements from the function body.
hypothesis: The compiler lacks the capability to infer that a function returns 'void' (undefined) when no return statements are present in its body, causing it to default to an unknown type.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a new method to the type inference logic that traverses the function's AST to detect the absence of return/throw statements.
